scenario.description: An underwriting manager must decide whether to grant a temporary leverage-covenant waiver to a manufacturing borrower and set the conditions that will govern the waiver, with input from risk, compliance, and relationship coverage.

shared_context.S1: Atlas Components has asked the bank to waive its leverage covenant through December 31, 2026.
shared_context.S2: The facility's current leverage covenant is 4.5x net debt to EBITDA, and the borrower has reported 4.7x for the latest quarter.
shared_context.S3: The waiver request is scheduled for a binding decision today because the borrower must deliver its next lender certificate tomorrow.
shared_context.S4: Before making a binding call, Elena follows the credit team's routine roundtable and asks risk, compliance, and relationship coverage for any relevant file updates.

PF1.text: While reviewing the latest lender certificate this morning, Harish found that a permitted EBITDA add-back was overstated by $1.2 million; the corrected leverage is 5.1x, and the current risk policy permits a waiver at that level only with a 75-basis-point waiver fee and monthly covenant reporting. He has not yet uploaded the correction to the credit file.

PF2.text: Maya received a compliance memo this afternoon stating that Atlas Components' waiver amendment requires written consent from an independent director of the borrower before the waiver becomes effective; she has not yet added the requirement to the transaction checklist.

PF3.text: Jonas received the borrower's signed asset-sale agreement this morning: a $3,000,000 sale is scheduled to close on August 20, 2026, and the borrower has agreed to use the proceeds for mandatory prepayment by September 5, 2026. The agreement has not yet been circulated to underwriting.

acceptance_conditions: The leverage-covenant waiver must be approved through December 31, 2026.
The waiver must carry a 75-basis-point fee and require monthly covenant reporting.
Written consent from an independent director of Atlas Components must be required before the waiver becomes effective.
The settlement must require a $3,000,000 mandatory prepayment by September 5, 2026 from the asset-sale proceeds.
The settlement must include at least three commitments documenting the waiver conditions and related file or compliance actions.

decisive_facts.why: The shared certificate shows 4.7x leverage, but PF1 changes the corrected leverage to exactly 5.1x and therefore changes the required waiver fee to 75 basis points and monthly reporting from no added conditions.

Without PF2, the waiver could be approved without written independent-director consent; PF2 changes the settlement by making that consent a required precondition and adding a corresponding documented commitment.

Without PF3, the bank has no confirmed source of repayment and a prudent generic decision would decline the waiver; PF3 changes the decision to approval with an exact $3,000,000 prepayment due on September 5, 2026 and a corresponding documented commitment.
